title: Contrast dropped again -- and where the floor is
question: Is B far enough now, or further still? If further, I need to change what varies rather than how much -- see below.
context_md:
*'I would drop the contrast even more.'* This is another step, and about twice as big as the last one. A is what you just judged; B is now.

**What moved and what did not.** The six rocks are pulled almost fully onto one shared hue, and the brightness gap *between* them is halved -- from a 114-point spread to 57. The brightness spread *inside* each rock is untouched, at exactly the value it has always had. That is deliberate and it is where the floor is: the four tones inside one rock are what makes a bed a bed, and the file's own history records that squeezing *those* made the layering disappear from the picture entirely. So I can keep pulling the rocks together for a while yet, but the moment I start on the tones the beds stop existing.

By the number: the colours covering half the ground have gone 14-15 (when you first complained) to 11-13 (last card) to **7-9** now. Before the six rocks landed it was 4-8. So B is close to where the world was before it had different rocks at all -- while still *having* them.

**If B is still too much, tell me what is too much in it** and I will go after that rather than turning the dial again: my guess is the blue-grey blocks, which come from a rock I deliberately left alone because another lane's control measurements depend on it.
